lines.japanese: 僕じゃない僕は、学校を出るとまっすぐ羽田の家へ帰宅した。
lines.english: The me who was not me left school and went straight home to the Haneda residence.

lines.japanese: 次元の狭間で漂流する僕は、柳木原にもグレタガルドにも往かず、意識のすりガラスを通して彼の見聞きする情景を覗いていた。
lines.english: Adrift between dimensions, I went neither to Yanagihara nor to Gretagard. Instead, through the frosted glass of consciousness, I watched what he saw and heard.

lines.japanese: 折しも彼はいま、僕のことを考えていた。
lines.english: As it happened, he was thinking of me just then.

lines.japanese: いや、逆かもしれない。彼が僕のことを考えているから、僕はこうして本来覗くことのできない領域に触れているのかもしれない。
lines.english: Or perhaps it was the reverse. Perhaps his thoughts of me were allowing me to touch a realm that should ordinarily have been closed to me.

lines.japanese: 「ただいまあ」
lines.english: “I’m hooome.”

lines.japanese: 僕の鍵を使って、彼は当り前のように羽田の家へあがりこんだ。
lines.english: Using my key, he let himself into the Haneda home as though it were the most natural thing in the world.

lines.japanese: 「お、おかえりなさい」
lines.english: “W-welcome home.”

lines.japanese: 居間に小鳩がいた。のり煎餅を手にこたつで丸まっていた。テレビからは小学生男児向けのバトルアニメが流れていた。
lines.english: Kobato was in the living room, curled up beneath the blanket of the heated table with a seaweed rice cracker in hand. On television, a battle anime for elementary-school boys was playing.

lines.japanese: 「どもー♪　たまにはお話でもしよっかー」
lines.english: “Hey there. ♪ How about we have a little talk for once?”

lines.japanese: 僕じゃない僕は迷わず敷居をまたぎ、ふう寒い寒いなどと言いながらこたつに膝を入れた。
lines.english: The me who was not me crossed the threshold without hesitation and slid his knees under the heated table, complaining cheerfully of the cold.
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese: らしからぬ行動に、僕の妹はすぐ不審を感じたようだ。期待と緊張のいりまじった表情で尋ねる。
lines.english: My sister immediately sensed something amiss in this uncharacteristic behavior. Expectation and tension mingled in her face as she asked:

lines.japanese: 「……だ、だれですか」
lines.english: “…W-who are you?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　ああ、ごめんごめん。なんか今日はバイトの気分じゃなかったから帰ってきちゃった。俺俺、鷲介鷲介」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, sorry, sorry. I just wasn’t in the mood for work today, so I came home. It’s me, it’s me—Shusuke, Shusuke.”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「うわぁお！　そんな分かりやすい声出さないでよ小鳩さん、おいちゃん傷付いちゃうでしょ」
lines.english: “Ouch! Don’t make your disappointment quite so obvious, Kobato. You’ll wound your poor uncle’s heart.”

lines.japanese: 「あ！　あっ！　いえ、そんなつもりではございませぬ」
lines.english: “Ah! N-no! Such was not my intent.”

lines.japanese: 「ん～？　なになに、やっぱ俺より、タカシお兄ちゃんに会いたかったわけ？」
lines.english: “Hmm? What’s this? You wanted to see your big brother Takashi instead of me?”

lines.japanese: 「や、それはべつに」
lines.english: “No. Not particularly.”

lines.japanese: 「だよねえ、そりゃあ俺なんかよりお兄ちゃんの方が……って、べつにかい！」
lines.english: “Of course. Why would you want me when you could have your big bro—wait, not particularly?!”

lines.japanese: 「だって……べつにあのひと、ほんとのお兄ちゃんじゃないし」
lines.english: “Because… he isn’t really my brother.”

lines.japanese: 「あらら、小鳩さんったら、あのひとだなんて他人行儀な呼び方しちゃってまあ」
lines.english: “My, my, Kobato. You make him sound like a perfect stranger.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、てかキミ、ふだんタカシ君のことなんて呼んでんの？　お兄ちゃん？　にいさん？　あんちゃん？　兄貴？　兄者？　兄上？　にーにー？」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, what do you usually call Takashi? Big brother? Brother? Bro? Big bro? Elder brother? Honored brother? Bubba?”

lines.japanese: 「ん……べつに……」
lines.english: “Mm… nothing in particular…”

lines.japanese: 「なに、べつにって」
lines.english: “What do you mean, nothing?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに、なんとも……」
lines.english: “I don’t call him anything…”

lines.japanese: 「え、え、どゆこと？」
lines.english: “What? How does that even work?”

lines.japanese: 「多少の会話なら『あの』とか『ねえ』で済みます」
lines.english: “For short conversations, ‘um’ or ‘hey’ is sufficient.”

lines.japanese: 「多少じゃない会話はどうすんの」
lines.english: “And what do you do when the conversation isn’t short?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ……したことないから分かんない」
lines.english: “I wouldn’t know… We have never had one.”

lines.japanese: 「ひどっ！　たまには兄妹じっくり語りあったらいいじゃない。可哀想に、彼はいまだに君のこと本当の妹だと思ってんのよ」
lines.english: “Cruel! You two ought to sit down and have a proper heart-to-heart once in a while. Poor guy—he still thinks you’re his real little sister.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、いいひと。きらいじゃないです。でも、やっぱり、お兄ちゃんだとは思えません」
lines.english: “Yes, he is a good person. I do not dislike him. But I still cannot think of him as my brother.”

lines.japanese: 「もー小鳩さんったら、また身持ちの固い未亡人みたいなこと言っちゃって。そんな言葉、もしタカシ君が聞いたら泣いちゃうどこの騒ぎじゃないよ？　どっか飛んでっちゃうよ？」
lines.english: “Oh, Kobato, there you go again, talking like some fiercely chaste widow. If Takashi heard you say that, crying would be the least of it. He’d fly away somewhere.”

lines.japanese: 「小鳩さんの気持ちも分かるけどさあ。でも、これからはタカシ君のことをお兄ちゃんだと思えって決めたのは、他でもないキミの“ホントのお兄ちゃん”なわけなんでしょ」
lines.english: “I understand how you feel. But the one who decided you should think of Takashi as your brother from now on was none other than your ‘real brother,’ wasn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん……だから努力はしています。ホントのお兄ちゃんが決めたことだから」
lines.english: “Yes… That is why I am trying. My real brother decided it.”

lines.japanese: 「はぁー、その健気さは無垢なる罪だねえ。タカシ君だいじょぶかな」
lines.english: “Ahh. Such brave devotion is innocence made sinful. I wonder if Takashi will survive.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえ小鳩さん、もしも俺と隼人君がぜんぶ彼に任せて消えたとしたら、キミ、この先タカシ君とふたりだけでやってける？」
lines.english: “Tell me, Kobato: if Hayato and I left everything to him and disappeared, could you and Takashi manage on your own from then on?”
“Hmm…”

lines.japanese: 「悩むなよ」
lines.english: “Don’t think about it that hard.”

lines.japanese: 「たぶん大丈夫だと思います」
lines.english: “I believe we would probably be all right.”

lines.japanese: 「本当に？」
lines.english: “You really think so?”

lines.japanese: 「あのひとをほんとのお兄ちゃんだとは思えないけど、同きょ人のおにいさんだと思うことにしています」
lines.english: “I cannot think of him as my real brother, but I have decided to think of him as an older boy who lives with me.”
“M-mmm…?”

lines.japanese: 「ごはんのときとか、ためになる話をいっぱいしてくれます。でも私は妹っぽくしなきゃってゆうのがあるから、いっつもきんちょうしちゃって、なかなか上手にしゃべれないです。でもがんばります」
lines.english: “At dinner, he tells me many useful things. But I feel I must behave like a little sister, so I am always nervous and can never speak very well. Still, I shall persevere.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そお？　まー、じゃー、それでいいか……」
lines.english: “Oh. Is that so? Well, then… I guess that’s good enough…”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さんたちはなんでですか」
lines.english: “Why do you and the others do it, Mr. Chitose?”

lines.japanese: 「ハイ？　なにが？」
lines.english: “Come again? Do what?”

lines.japanese: 「あのひとの将来とか、びょういん代とかのために、おしごとしてお金をためてあげてるのはなんでですか」
lines.english: “Why do you work and save money for his future, and for his hospital bills?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それはね……」
lines.english: “Ah. Well, you see…”

lines.japanese: 「なんでって言われると、まあ、彼が長男でうちらが弟だから、っていう答えになるかな」
lines.english: “When you ask why… I suppose the answer is that he’s the eldest son, and the rest of us are his younger brothers.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅーん……？」
lines.english: “I see…?”

lines.japanese: 「小鳩さんだって、なんでペットは可愛がらなきゃいけないのか、なんで総理大臣は偉いのかって、そんなの深く考えたことないでしょ。そーゆーもんだって、物心つくころには当たり前に教えられてたでしょ」
lines.english: “You’ve probably never stopped to wonder why you’re supposed to love a pet, or why the prime minister is important. By the time you were old enough to know anything, you’d already been taught that was simply the way of the world.”

lines.japanese: 「うちらにとってタカシ君はそういう存在だったの。そんだけかな、少なくとも最初の理由は」
lines.english: “That’s what Takashi was to us. At least, that was the reason at first.”

lines.japanese: 「いまのりゆうは違うんですか」
lines.english: “Is the reason different now?”

lines.japanese: 「そうねえ、根本的にはそれなんだけど、そのうちに贖罪って意味合いも加わったかな」
lines.english: “Fundamentally it’s the same, but somewhere along the way, I suppose atonement became part of it too.”

lines.japanese: 「しょくざい？」
lines.english: “Atonement?”

lines.japanese: 「平たく言えば罪ほろぼしってことね。んー、なんてーのかな……えっとねえ、本人に自覚はないだろうけど、ぶっちゃけ彼は可哀想な子なのよ」
lines.english: “In plain terms, making amends for our sins. How do I put this…? He probably doesn’t realize it himself, but honestly, he’s a poor, unfortunate kid.”

lines.japanese: 「は？　はー」
lines.english: “What? Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、それはある意味、うちらのせいでさ」
lines.english: “And in a certain sense, that is our fault.”

lines.japanese: 「なにかやらかしましたか」
lines.english: “Did you do something terrible?”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、どう説明したらいいかな……うーん、どのみち観念的な話になっちゃうんで、最初からたとえ話でいっとくね。昔々あるところに、自称・弱っちい神様がいました」
lines.english: “Let me see. How can I explain this…? Hmm. It’s bound to get abstract either way, so I’ll make it a parable from the start. Once upon a time, there lived a self-proclaimed weak little god.”

lines.japanese: 「弱っちい自分じゃ大事なお姫様を守れないと思った神様は、あるとき、何があってもへこたれない無敵の自分を作ることにしました」
lines.english: “The god believed that, weak as he was, he could never protect his precious princess. So one day he decided to create another self—an invincible self whom nothing could ever discourage.”

lines.japanese: 「やー、でも、神様まだ子供だからねー。なんていうかね。負けたと思わなければ勝てなくても無敵、ていうね。そう単純に思っちゃったんだろうね」
lines.english: “But the god was still a child, you see. How should I put it? ‘Even if I never win, I’m invincible as long as I never think I’ve lost.’ He must have thought it was as simple as that.”

lines.japanese: 「かくして痛みを知らない子供は生まれましたとさ」
lines.english: “And thus a child who knew no pain was born. The end.”

lines.japanese: 「はー……よく分かんないけど、それがあのひとですか？」
lines.english: “I do not entirely understand… but is that child him?”

lines.japanese: 「んもう、だから小鳩さんってば水臭いわ。お兄ちゃんって呼んであげてちょうだいな……ああ、いやいや、これはたとえ話なんで。べつにタカシ君とかヨージ君とか関係ないんで。おーけい？」
lines.english: “Honestly, Kobato, you’re so distant. Do be a dear and call him your brother… Ah, no, no. This is only a parable. It has absolutely nothing to do with Takashi or Yoji. Okay?”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん、わかった……」
lines.english: “Y-yes. I understand…”

lines.japanese: 「でもさあホラ、痛みは危険を知らせる大事なシグナルなんてよく言うでしょ」
lines.english: “But you know how people say pain is an important signal warning us of danger?”

lines.japanese: 「考えてみてよ。もし怪我したり手ぇ切ったり内臓こわしたりしたとき、痛みがなかったらどうなる？　それで体がよくなるわけじゃないんだから、気付かないままどんどん悪化しちゃうでしょ」
lines.english: “Think about it. Suppose you were injured, cut your hand, or damaged an organ. What would happen if you felt no pain? The lack of pain wouldn’t heal your body. The damage would simply grow worse and worse while you remained unaware.”

lines.japanese: 「それはカラダでもココロでも同じだったんだよねえ。痛覚マヒしてホーク無敵ィ～なんつって喜んでる場合じゃなかったわけ。それは看過せざるべき重篤な異状なんだよ」
lines.english: “The same went for body and mind. This was no time to celebrate, ‘My pain's switched off—Hawk is invincible!’ It was a grave disorder that couldn't be ignored.”

lines.japanese: 「ね？　なかなかヒドイ話でしょ。可哀想だと思わない？」
lines.english: “You see? It’s a fairly awful story. Don’t you feel sorry for him?”

lines.japanese: 「よ、よく分かりませんが、なんとなく大変そうです」
lines.english: “I-I do not quite understand, but it sounds terribly difficult.”

lines.japanese: 「そ。大変だったの。だから無意識のうち限界に達していた彼は、ココロに傷を負うと、それを中和するために記憶や思考を改竄するようになりました。ああ、たとえば、例のグレタガルドの救世主とかって設定ね」
lines.english: “It was. He had reached his limit without even realizing it. So whenever his heart was wounded, he began altering his memories and thoughts to neutralize the hurt. For example, that business about being the savior of Gretagard.”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、いわゆる現実とうひですか」
lines.english: “Um… what people call escapism?”

lines.japanese: 「言っちゃえばそうなるけど。傷付いたり悲しんだりが許されなかったから、そうするしかなかったのね」
lines.english: “That’s what it amounts to. He wasn’t permitted to be hurt or sad, so it was the only thing he could do.”

lines.japanese: 「彼が飛んじゃってるあいだの場つなぎとして、神様はさらに新しい自分を作ってゆくわけだけど、次以降にはちゃんと痛みを感じる機能も付けてるんだ」
lines.english: “The god went on creating new selves to fill the gaps while the boy was away. But from the next one onward, he made certain to give them the ability to feel pain.”

lines.japanese: 「つまりね、俺や隼人君が壊れないで済んでるのは、タカシ君っていう悲しい教訓があったからなの」
lines.english: “In other words, the reason Hayato and I have managed not to break is that we had Takashi as a sorrowful lesson.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うーん、よくわかんないや」
lines.english: “I… Hmm. I still do not understand.”

lines.japanese: 「あれえ？　そう？　えー、約束の日もそう遠くないと思って、長年言ってなかったコトけっこー赤裸々に語っちゃったつもりなんだけど……小鳩さんにはまだ早かったかなあ」
lines.english: “Huh? Really? Uh, I thought the appointed day wasn’t too far off, so I figured I’d been pretty open about stuff I hadn’t talked about in years… Maybe it was still too soon for you, Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 「自己さいてんですが、きまつテストの国語は８０点以上いってるっぽいです」
lines.english: “According to my own marking, I appear to have scored at least eighty on the Japanese final.”

lines.japanese: 「はあはあ、読解力には問題ないと。そっかー、じゃあこっちの話し方が悪かったんだねー。ごめんねー」
lines.english: “Yes, yes, your reading comprehension is beyond reproach. I see. Then I must have explained it badly. So sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「気にしないでください。ひょうげん力は作文をいっぱいやれば上がると平賀せんせいがゆってました」
lines.english: “Please do not concern yourself. Ms. Hiraga says one’s powers of expression improve if one writes a great many compositions.”

lines.japanese: 「わあ、ほーんと？　ようし、じゃあ米田さんからいっぱい仕事もらってがんばっちゃうぞーう」
lines.english: “Oh, really? All right, then! I’ll get Ms. Yoneda to give me piles of work, and I’ll practice my little heart out!”

lines.japanese: 「なんつって？　やー、どうかねえ？　うちら、これから出てくる機会だんだん減ってくると思うけど」
lines.english: “Or something. Still… who knows? I think the rest of us will have fewer and fewer chances to appear from here on.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　そーなんですか？」
lines.english: “What? Is that true?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、おそらくね。タカシ君のガッツ次第なとこあるけど、俺と隼人君はそう考えてたんだ。少しずつ≪コックピット≫に入ってる時間を長くさせて……って感じで」
lines.english: “Probably. It depends on Takashi’s nerve, but that’s what Hayato and I had in mind: gradually letting him spend longer and longer in the *Cockpit*.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ほら。彼って、うちらのせいで慢性的に寝不足でしょ。それがまずよくないと思わない？　寝不足は万病の素だもん」
lines.english: “You know how chronically sleep-deprived he is because of us? Don’t you agree that’s the first thing we need to fix? Lack of sleep is the root of every illness.”

lines.japanese: 「寝なきゃ育ちません。けんぜんな子が育まれません。保健の大塚先生がゆってました」
lines.english: “You can't grow if you don't sleep. Healthy children cannot be raised without it. Ms. Otsuka from health class said so.”

lines.japanese: 「でしょお？　うん、じゃあ、おいちゃん寝かせてくるね、この体。ばいばい小鳩さん、おやすみー」
lines.english: “Exactly. So your uncle is going to put this body to bed. Bye-bye, Kobato. Good night.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん、おやすみなさ──」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes, good ni—”

lines.japanese: 「──えっ、ああああの、晩ごはんは食べないんですか」
lines.english: “—w-wait! Aren’t you going to eat dinner?”

lines.japanese: 「あら、嬉しいお誘い。小鳩さんの手作り？」
lines.english: “Why, what a delightful invitation. Did you make it yourself?”

lines.japanese: 「レンジでチンもふくみます」
lines.english: “Heating things in the microwave is included.”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、最近のレトルトは美味しいからねえ」
lines.english: “Well, ready-made meals are pretty good these days.”

lines.japanese: 「れいとう食品もあなどれぬそんざいです」
lines.english: “Frozen food is also a presence not to be underestimated.”

lines.japanese: 「いやっほう、その通り！　ああでもごめんなさい、今日は遠慮しときましょう、麗しのプリンセス・ダヴ。今ひとの温もりに触れると、行きづらくなっちゃいそうで。またいつか、機会があれば」
lines.english: “Precisely! Ah, but forgive me. Tonight I must decline, my lovely Princess Dove. If I touch another person’s warmth just now, I fear leaving will become rather difficult. Another time, if the chance arises.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん、分かった。お待ちしてます」
lines.english: “Y-yes, I understand. I shall be waiting.”
“Ah…”

lines.japanese: 「楽しいなあ……」
lines.english: “What fun…”

lines.japanese: 「おやすみ、この素晴らしき世界……」
lines.english: “Good night, you wonderful world…”

lines.japanese: 「はあああーっ！」
lines.english: “Haaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「いやああああーっ！」
lines.english: “Yaaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「でえェェェりゃあァァァァァっ！」
lines.english: “Hrrrraaaaaagh!”

lines.japanese: グレタガルド。
lines.english: Gretagard.

lines.japanese: 僕の居場所。
lines.english: The place where I belonged.

lines.japanese: 僕の世界。
lines.english: My world.

lines.japanese: 僕だけの──世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: Mine alone—*may peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: 「貴様ら皆殺しだああああああ！！」
lines.english: “I’ll slaughter every last one of you!”

lines.japanese: 「うあ゛あアぁぁあ゛あ゛ああああぁぁアアアぁ──ッ！！」
lines.english: “Rrrraaaaaaaaagh!”

lines.japanese: 「あ゛アァああッ！　はアッ、ハアッ！　うわああ゛アぁぁぁああーッ！」
lines.english: “Aaaagh! Hah, hah! Raaaaaagh!”

lines.japanese: 世界の平和を守るため涙も拭わず戦う僕を、どこかで誰かが嗤っていた。
lines.english: Somewhere, someone was laughing at me as I fought to protect the peace of the world without even stopping to wipe away my tears.
